legal_sources.title: Ohio Revised Code — Ohio Rev. Code § 1923.081 — Joinder of claims.

challenges.judge_assessment: The challenge is established. The cited statutory text addresses joinder and trial of a plaintiff's rent and damages claims in a forcible-entry-and-detainer action; it does not support the attributed assertion that public policy requires excluding the Rules of Civil Procedure from forcible-entry actions. The quotation or attribution must be corrected before filing.
challenges.suggested_response: In Haney, supra, the court of appeals concluded that a tenant need not file a counterclaim in a forcible entry and detainer action because "Civ.R. 13(A) does not apply in forcible entry and detainer actions to require tenants to assert compulsory counterclaims."
challenges.coaching_recommendation: Delete the unsupported public-policy assertion and do not attribute to R.C. 1923.081 a tenant’s right to reserve later claims unless Haney itself is properly cited and verified for that proposition.

challenges.reason: Sherman identifies the issue as whether the tenant's personal-injury claim was a compulsory counterclaim in the landlord's earlier forcible-entry-and-detainer-and-rent action, and holds that it was compulsory under Civ.R. 13(A).
challenges.sourcePassage: “This appeal presents a single issue: whether the personal-injury claim of the plaintiff-appellant, Adrienne Sherman, ... was a compulsory counterclaim which she was required to assert ... in the landlord’s earlier action against her for forcible entry and detainer and rent. We hold that ... Sherman’s personal injury claim was a compulsory counterclaim, and therefore summary judgment for the landlord was properly granted.”

challenges.reason: Haney reproduces the quoted definition of a summary proceeding in its discussion of Ohio forcible-entry-and-detainer procedure. The supplied source does not provide reliable page boundaries for independently measuring the pinpoint, which was designated unmeasured.
challenges.sourcePassage: “A summary proceeding is one where the trial is conducted promptly and simply, without the aid of a jury and without strict observance of all the rules which normally govern civil proceedings.”

challenges.challenge: R.C. 1923.081 addresses joinder and trial of rent-and-damages claims with a forcible-entry-and-detainer action; the retrieved statutory text does not support the additional quoted assertion that public policy requires exclusion of the civil rules from forcible-entry actions.
challenges.reason: The statute's retrieved text concerns the optional inclusion of a landlord's rent and damage claims in the forcible-entry-and-detainer trial. It does not state the quoted public-policy rationale about excluding the Rules of Civil Procedure. Thus, the citation does not support the full quotation attributed to the statute.
challenges.sourcePassage: “A trial in an action for forcible entry and detainer for residential premises ... pursuant to this chapter may also include a trial on claims of the plaintiff for past due rent and other damages under a rental agreement, unless for good cause shown the court continues the trial on those claims.”
